slides.title: Vanity Metrics Say Little About Real Value
bullets: Followers, views and clicks are easy to obtain
They say little about actual scientific value generated
Real measurement connects activity to understanding, relationship, decisions
The same leap already required for medical KPIs elsewhere

slides.title: Activity Metrics Confirm Reach, Not Impact
bullets: Open rates, clicks, view time and completion are useful process signals
They confirm content arrives and gets some interaction
Relying on them alone gives an incomplete picture
Risks optimizing for what's easy to measure, not what matters

slides.title: Does the Journey Actually Deepen?
bullets: Does an HCP move from introductory to deeper content
Does digital content show up as more informed questions in visits
Does combining channels build more relationship and trust over time
Compares real journey quality, not isolated channel activity

slides.title: The Hardest Link: Content to Practice
bullets: Tries to connect digital exposure to real changes in clinical practice
Still the least established level in current industry practice
Requires careful evaluation design
Shares the same causal attribution limits as any impact narrative

slides.title: Judge Tools by Impact, Not Reach
bullets: Understand these levels beyond surface reach numbers
Assess the real effectiveness of digital tools you recommend
Bring field perspective so teams prioritize impact over volume

takeaway.title: Real digital measurement moves past vanity metrics toward journey quality and practice impact
bullets: Open rates and clicks confirm reach but not scientific value
Journey-level metrics show whether interest is genuinely deepening
Linking digital exposure to practice change is the hardest, rarest level
